findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs, which breaks under JSON task serialization
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound calls sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async with kwargs containing assignment_source.to_dict(), and to_dict() (via dataclasses.asdict) includes the 'queued' field as a datetime object. If the Celery broker/worker uses JSON task serialization, serializing these kwargs raises TypeError, which propagates up through GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign and fails the entire inbound webhook assignment (including the DB-side effects if inside a transaction). Even when pickle is used, the round-trip through from_dict is inconsistent: a JSON-serialized 'queued' comes back as a string that is never validated or coerced. Since 'queued' is never read anywhere, the simplest fix is to remove the field, or serialize it as an ISO string.

findings.title: Dataclass default 'queued: datetime = timezone.now()' is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The default value for the 'queued' field is computed when the class definition is executed (module import time), not when an instance is created. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit 'queued' therefore carries the same import-time timestamp, making the field misleading if it is ever used for staleness/observability. It should be declared with dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now). The added test (assert result.get('queued') is not None) passes either way and does not catch this.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound abstract signature gains an unused 'assignment_source' parameter with inconsistent naming
findings.body: The abstract sync_status_outbound now accepts assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None, but no caller in this PR ever passes it, no implementation is updated to use it, and status syncing has no assignment-source cycle-breaking logic (should_sync is never called with a source for status keys). It also uses a different parameter name ('assignment_source') than the sibling should_sync method ('sync_source') for the same concept. This is dead, misleading API surface: either wire status sync through the same source-checking path or drop the parameter until it is implemented.

findings.title: No test that a different integration still receives outbound assignee sync when an assignment_source is set
findings.body: The new test only covers the suppression case (assignment_source matching the target integration blocks sync). The core guarantee stated in the should_sync comment — 'This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward' — is untested: there is no test where a group is linked to external issues from two integrations, an inbound change sourced from integration A is applied, and the outbound sync to integration B still fires. A regression that over-suppresses (e.g., comparing against the wrong id or dropping the source check entirely for non-matching cases) would not be caught by the current test suite.
